display.purpose: The name only; size is calc(var(--scene-px) * 32.64), so 131px at a 4px scene scale and about 98px at 3px.

item.purpose: Ledger row content: trades and band names. The largest type below the hero.

body.purpose: The note above the bands and default text.

label.purpose: Ledger row labels only: 21.76px (16.32px below 46rem), uppercase, one glyph pixel (0.092em) of tracking, ink-soft.

shadows.name: meter-cap
shadows.purpose: Not elevation: an unblurred inset that paints the frost top pixel of each level-meter bar.

motion.name: scene-frame
motion.purpose: Aurora drift, star twinkle, snowfall, chimney smoke, water ripple, lamp-reflection flicker. Paused offscreen and when the tab is hidden.

motion.name: shooting-star
motion.purpose: One frost-ice-glacier streak across the upper sky, on the scene's 10fps clock.

motion.name: level-meter
motion.value: steps(1, end), 1.1s to 1.9s per bar, staggered negative delays
motion.purpose: Seven bars jump between whole scene-pixel heights (2 to 10); never eased.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: single still frame (t = 4s); meter animation none
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce renders one scene frame and holds the meter bars at their resting heights.

motion.name: resize-debounce
motion.purpose: Scene and shore re-layout after resize.

breakpoints.name: ledger-two-column
breakpoints.value: min-width 46rem: each row splits into an 11rem label column and the content; band grid goes to three columns

breakpoints.name: bands-one-column
breakpoints.value: max-width 23rem: band grid drops to one column (two otherwise)

breakpoints.name: portrait
breakpoints.value: hero height > 1.15 x width: horizon at 60%, nameplate on the water

components.name: Nameplate
components.description: The name alone, set directly on the night sky; no role line, glyph, panel, or scrim.
components.css: .ds-nameplate { background: #0f2b4c; padding: 3rem 2rem; font-family: "Pixelify Sans", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; } .ds-name { margin: 0; font-weight: 400; font-size: 131px; line-height: 0.9; color: #f3f3f3; } .ds-nameplate ::selection { background: #e3f2fd; color: #0f2b4c; }

components.name: Ledger
components.description: Rows of ink-soft uppercase labels beside snow item-size content, one label column and one content edge, ridge-blue pixel-dot rules between rows; items each led by a 9x9 ice glyph.
components.html:

Before
MusicProgramming
components.css: .ds-ledger { margin: 0; padding: 2.5rem 2rem; max-width: 64rem; background: #0f2b4c; font-family: "Pixelify Sans", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; } .ds-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 0.75rem; padding: clamp(1.5rem, 4vh, 2.25rem) 0; background: linear-gradient(90deg, #1c3b5e 50%, transparent 0) left top / 8px 4px repeat-x; } .ds-row:first-child { background: none; padding-top: 0; } @media (min-width: 46rem) { .ds-row { grid-template-columns: 11rem minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 0 clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem); align-items: baseline; } } .ds-row dt { color: #c4d3e0; font-size: 21.76px; line-height: 1.5; letter-spacing: 0.092em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-row dd { margin: 0; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem clamp(1.5rem, 4vw, 3rem); font-size: 32.64px; line-height: 1.2; color: #f3f3f3; } .ds-item { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.45em; } .ds-glyph { width: 36px; height: 36px; flex: none; fill: #90caf9; shape-rendering: crispEdges; } .ds-ledger ::selection { background: #e3f2fd; color: #0f2b4c; }

components.name: Pixel Glyph
components.description: 9x9 grids of unit squares in ice: gear, note, prompt. Nine scene pixels square (36px at a 4px scale); decorative, one per ledger item.
components.css: .ds-glyphs { display: flex; gap: 12px; padding: 1.5rem 2rem; background: #0f2b4c; } .ds-px { width: 36px; height: 36px; fill: #90caf9; shape-rendering: crispEdges; }

components.name: Level Meter
components.description: Seven ice bars with frost cap pixels under the Listening label, jumping between whole scene-pixel heights with steps() timing; still under reduced motion.
components.css: .ds-meter-wrap { padding: 1.5rem 2rem; background: #0f2b4c; font-family: "Pixelify Sans", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; } .ds-label { display: block; color: #c4d3e0; font-size: 21.76px; line-height: 1.5; letter-spacing: 0.092em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-eq { --b: 4px; display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: var(--b); height: calc(var(--b) * 10); margin-top: 0.9rem; } .ds-eq i { width: calc(var(--b) * 2); height: calc(var(--b) * var(--h, 3)); background: #90caf9; box-shadow: inset 0 var(--b) 0 #e3f2fd; animation: ds-level 1.6s steps(1, end) infinite; } .ds-eq i:nth-child(1) { --h: 4; animation-duration: 1.3s; } .ds-eq i:nth-child(2) { --h: 7; animation-duration: 1.7s; animation-delay: -0.4s; } .ds-eq i:nth-child(3) { --h: 5; animation-duration: 1.1s; animation-delay: -0.9s; } .ds-eq i:nth-child(4) { --h: 9; animation-duration: 1.9s; animation-delay: -0.2s; } .ds-eq i:nth-child(5) { --h: 6; animation-duration: 1.4s; animation-delay: -1.1s; } .ds-eq i:nth-child(6) { --h: 8; animation-duration: 1.2s; animation-delay: -0.6s; } .ds-eq i:nth-child(7) { --h: 3; animation-duration: 1.8s; animation-delay: -1.3s; } @keyframes ds-level { 0% { height: calc(var(--b) * var(--h)); } 25% { height: calc(var(--b) * 2); } 50% { height: calc(var(--b) * 10); } 75% { height: calc(var(--b) * 5); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-eq i { animation: none; } }

components.name: Dithered Sky Band

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "One Polar Night"**

The whole page is a single night by a fjord. The first viewport is the place itself: a procedural pixel-art canvas of aurora, a crescent moon, falling snow, a layered alpine range anchored by one tall horn peak, forested foothills, a pine shore with one lit cabin, and still water that reflects all of it. Nothing sits on top of the scene as a banner or card; the name is set straight into the sky (or, on portrait screens, onto the dark water at the scene's foot). Scrolling continues down into the water, which settles into the page field so the introduction reads as text under the waterline, and the page closes on a second, smaller canvas: a snowy pine bank, the far shore.

Below the waterline the introduction is one ledger: a few rows, each a small label beside its content, separated by rows of square pixel dots. One label column and one content edge hold every row, so the eye runs straight down. Small pixel marks drawn on the scene's grid (9x9 glyphs, square markers, a stepped level meter) give the text a little of the night's life. The atmosphere carries the personality: cold blues, hard pixel edges, ordered-dither tones, and exactly one warm light, which lives only in the scene. Hierarchy comes from size in one pixel face at one weight. There are no links, controls, borders, shadows-as-depth, or containers; the system is made of a field, two scenes, type, and a few pixel marks.

The direction contract still names a lamplight text mark; it was removed from the build at the user's request, and the build is the record here.
keyCharacteristics: Canvas scenes drawn at a whole-number art-pixel scale (3 or 4 screen px per art pixel) and upscaled with crisp, pixelated edges; the hero scene opens the page and a shore canvas closes it.
Dark fjord set as ground; the ice-blue set is light: the sky, plus a few small pixel marks in the text.
One warm accent, the cabin's lamplight, and only inside the scene.
One face (Pixelify Sans, 400) across every role; size is the main hierarchy lever.
One ledger below the scene: a fixed label column, one content edge, pixel-dot rules between rows.
Square everything: no radius, no card, no border; rules and markers are square pixels on the scene grid.
Quiet, stepped motion (the scene at 10 frames a second, the meter by whole-pixel jumps), paused offscreen and frozen for reduced-motion users.

rules.name: The One Warm Light Rule
rules.body: Lamplight amber and ember appear only in the cabin window and its reflection on the water. Every other color on the page, scene and text alike, is cold. A second warm element breaks the night.

rules.name: The Ice Is Light Rule
rules.body: The ice-blue set (frost, ice, glacier, abyss) is light, never ground. It belongs to the sky (aurora, stars, moon, snowfall, shooting star, snow crests, glints) and, in the text layer, only to small pixel marks: the 9x9 glyphs, the band markers, and the level meter, with frost as the meter's cap pixel and the selection highlight. Words, labels, and surfaces stay in snow, ink-soft, and night.

rules.name: The One Face, One Weight Rule
rules.body: Every role is Pixelify Sans at 400. Hierarchy is made by size (and ink-soft versus snow), never by bold, italics, or a second family. Uppercase and tracking belong to the ledger label alone.

rules.name: The Name on the Grid Rule
rules.body: The display size is derived from the scene's pixel scale so the name's pixels align with the art's pixels. Never set the name in a free fluid size that breaks that lock.

rules.name: The One Edge Rule
rules.body: Every ledger row shares one label column and one content edge. New facts join the ledger as rows; they do not open a second layout.

rules.name: The Depth Is Distance Rule
rules.body: Separation comes from atmospheric value steps in the scene and from space on the page, never from drop shadows, overlays, or raised surfaces.

rules.name: The Dithered Sky Rule
rules.body: Sky, aurora, and haze tones change only through a 4x4 ordered (Bayer) dither between palette steps, at whole art pixels; never a smooth CSS or canvas gradient. The water is the one exception: its mirror blends the reflection into the fjord tint row by row, still on whole art pixels, and its last fifth dithers out into the night field.

dos: Do keep the page field night and every surface flat; the canvases are the only images.
Do draw any new pixel art on the same whole-number art-pixel grid (3 or 4 screen px) with `image-rendering: pixelated`, and size small marks in multiples of the scene pixel.
Do step sky, aurora, and haze tones with ordered dither between palette colors.
Do set every text role in Pixelify Sans 400 and build hierarchy by size, using snow for primary text and ink-soft for secondary.
Do keep layout left-aligned inside the fluid gutter, with generous viewport-scaled vertical space; add new facts as ledger rows on the shared label column.
Do keep motion slow and stepped (10fps for the scene, `steps()` timing for CSS), pause it offscreen, and hold it still for reduced-motion users.
Do draw rules as rows of square pixel dots in ridge blue.
donts: Don't use lamplight amber or ember anywhere beyond the cabin window and its reflection.
Don't use the ice-blue set for words, labels, or surfaces; in the text layer it is only for small pixel marks.
Don't round corners, add drop shadows, or put content in cards, panels, or bordered boxes.
Don't use smooth gradients for sky, aurora, or haze tones.
Don't draw rules with `border` or the browser's round dotted style.
Don't add bold weights, italics, or a second typeface, or use uppercase tracking anywhere but the ledger label.
Don't center the name over the scene or place it on a scrim; it sits on the sky (or, on portrait screens, on the water).
